articles.title: South Africa’s Jansen claims top spots in two ICC Men’s Test Player Rankings
articles.text:
South Africa all-rounder Marco Jansen has attained No. 1 position in the bowlers’ and all-rounders’ rankings after playing a stellar role in his team’s huge innings and 31 runs victory over Australia in the second match of their ICC World Test Championship series.
Jansen’s gritty knock of 85 and hauls of five for 33 and one for 34 have, in fact, helped him advance in all three lists of the ICC Men’s Test Player Rankings as he has also gained 13 places to reach 56 th position among batters. Jansen is the first South Africa bowler to occupy the top spot since Kagiso Rabada in November 2024 and the first from his country to become the top-ranked Test all-rounder since Vernon Philander in August 2014.
Captain Temba Bavuma has also made huge progress after his match-winning 179 lifted him four slots to a career-best second position. He is now only behind England’s Harry Brook and with a chance to become the first South Africa player to top the Test batting rankings since A.B. de Villiers in November 2015.
Others to move up the Test rankings include Australia fast bowler Scott Boland, who is up three places to sixth position for a haul of five for 81 while South Africa’s Wiaan Mulder is up 10 places to 43 rd after finishing with five wickets across the two innings.
Abhishek returns as No. 1 in T20Is: India’s left-handed opener Abhishek Sharma’s blistering 35-ball century against New Zealand in Wellington on Tuesday has lifted him back to No. 1 position in the ICC Men’s T20I Batting Rankings with his team-mate Ishan Kishan slipping to third after occupying top position for four months. This is the second stint at the top for Abhishek, who was No. 1 from July 2025 to June this year.
Sanju Samson (up six places to 20 th ), Finn Allen (up three places to 25 th ) and Glenn Phillips (up 20 places to 37 th ) are among the others to move up the list for their performances in the ongoing series in New Zealand while the home side’s captain Mitchell Santner (up seven places to seventh), and India pace bowlers Arshdeep Singh (up six places to 15 th ) and Prince Yadav (up 19 places to 83 rd ) have progressed in the bowling rankings.
The ICC Men’s ODI Player Rankings see England batters Ben Duckett and Brook advance six places each to seventh and eight positions for their knocks in the Pakistan ODI Tri-Series also featuring Sri Lanka. Duckett scored 105 against Pakistan and Brook recorded the fastest double century in the format against Sri Lanka, but both knocks were in losing causes.
Shadab Khan, who helped Pakistan to a one-run victory in Lahore against England with an unbeaten 113, has moved up 32 places to 92 nd while Janith Liyanage of Sri Lanka (up 10 places to 14 th ), Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza (up seven places to 20 th ), Namibia captain Gerhard Erasmus (up 15 places to 45 th ) and the Netherlands’ Max O’Dowd (up seven places to 55 th ) are others to move up among ODI batters.
The ODI bowling rankings see Afghanistan’s Azmatullah Omarzai (up 13 places to seventh), Namibia’s Vernard Scholtz (up nine places to eighth), Sri Lanka’s Dumith Wellalage (up eight places to 19 th ) and Afghanistan’s Mohammad Nabi (up 14 places to 27 th ) make notable gains. Nabi has also moved up five places to third among all-rounders.

articles.summary: South Africa all-rounder Marco Jansen has attained No. 1 position in the bowlers’ and all-rounders’ rankings after playing a stellar role in his team’s huge innings and 31 runs victory over Australia in the second match of their ICC World Test Championship series.

articles.title: Plans to establish vocational technology university in Polonnaruwa using Indian-funded buildings
articles.text:
The government is considering establishing a Vocational Technology University in the North Central Province by converting partially completed buildings originally constructed for a trilingual school in Kaduruwela, Polonnaruwa, with assistance from the Indian government.
According to the Ministry of Vocational Education, a site inspection and special discussion were held at the Polonnaruwa District Secretariat to explore transferring the buildings to the Ministry for the proposed university.
The buildings were partially constructed with Indian government assistance and subsequently handed over to the Sri Lankan government.
The discussion, chaired by Deputy Minister of Vocational Education Nalin Hewage, was attended by Speaker Dr. Jagath Wickramaratne, Deputy Minister of Water Supply T.B. Sarath, MP Padmasiri Bandara, Polonnaruwa District Secretary Sudantha Ekanayake and other senior government officials.
Officials reviewed the current condition of the buildings, their suitability for vocational education and the need to expand higher education opportunities for young people in the North Central Province.
Following the discussion, all parties agreed to proceed with the necessary steps to transfer the buildings to the Ministry of Vocational Education and establish the proposed university.
The initiative forms part of a broader government plan to establish vocational technology universities across all nine provinces, providing students with opportunities to progress from vocational training to degree-level qualifications.
The proposed university is expected to expand access to higher vocational education within the North Central Province and help develop skilled workers to meet labour market demands.
The Ministry said the programme aims to create a continuous educational pathway from vocational training to university degrees, with priority given to students from the respective provinces.
articles.summary: The government is considering establishing a Vocational Technology University in the North Central Province by converting partially completed buildings originally constructed for a trilingual school in Kaduruwela, Polonnaruwa, with assistance from the Indian government.

articles.title: Apple confirms screen problems in some newly launched foldable iPhone Duo
articles.text:
Apple has acknowledged display problems affecting a small number of its newly launched iPhone Duo foldable smartphones and announced that affected devices will be replaced.
According to Reuters, the issue emerged just days after Apple’s first foldable iPhone began reaching customers, with several users reporting cracks and lines appearing on the inner display near the central folding hinge.
The iPhone Duo, which opens like a passport booklet, began shipping last week following strong demand that saw initial online orders sell out within minutes.
In a statement issued on Monday, Apple confirmed that a limited number of devices were experiencing display problems.
“We are aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units,” Apple said.
The company advised customers experiencing display problems to contact AppleCare for a replacement.
Apple has not disclosed the cause of the issue or the total number of devices affected.
Meanwhile, repair specialist iFixit said its preliminary analysis suggested that a component within the phone’s folding mechanism could be creating pressure on the inner display.
The company used teardown footage, patents and CT scans to develop a three-dimensional simulation of the hinge mechanism.
Its findings suggested that a central support bar might not be moving sufficiently out of the screen’s way when the device is folded, potentially creating a stress point near the reported damage.
However, Apple has not confirmed this explanation.
Despite the reported problems, iFixit described the iPhone Duo as the most repairable foldable smartphone it has tested.
Technology analysts say Apple’s decision to offer replacements is an important early response to concerns surrounding its first foldable smartphone.
The development comes as Apple enters the foldable smartphone market, where competitors including Samsung have already introduced several generations of devices.
articles.summary: Apple has acknowledged display problems affecting a small number of its newly launched iPhone Duo foldable smartphones and announced that affected devices will be replaced. According to Reuters, the issue emerged just days after Apple’s first foldable iPhone began reaching customers, with several users reporting cracks and lines appearing on the inner display near the central folding hinge.

articles.title: Police clarify Media Spokesperson’s remarks on Homagama suspect’s death
articles.text:
Sri Lanka Police has rejected reports claiming that the Police Media Spokesperson stated that a suspect arrested with ICE narcotics in Homagama died due to an illness that occurred during a drug raid.
In a statement, Police clarified that the reports circulating in the media had falsely attributed such remarks to the Police Media Spokesperson.
The clarification relates to the death of a 29-year-old suspect arrested by Homagama Police officers with ICE at Pitipana Junction on October 25, 2026.
According to Police, the suspect had suddenly fallen ill after being brought to the Homagama Police Station following his arrest.
He was subsequently admitted to the Homagama Base Hospital for medical treatment, where he later died.
Police stated that the Media Spokesperson had issued a press release based on preliminary information received from the Homagama Police Station and had not claimed that the suspect fell ill during the drug raid.
The Police Media Division further explained that information released to the media is based on initial details provided by the relevant police stations or divisions.
Police urged the public to refrain from circulating misleading or distorted information before official medical reports are released or any suspicious circumstances requiring further investigation are established.
articles.summary: Sri Lanka Police has rejected reports claiming that the Police Media Spokesperson stated that a suspect arrested with ICE narcotics in Homagama died due to an illness that occurred during a drug raid. In a statement, Police clarified that the reports circulating in the media had falsely attributed such remarks to the Police Media Spokesperson.

articles.title: Customs seizes narcotics worth over Rs. 60 million in foreign postal parcels
articles.text:
Sri Lanka Customs has seized narcotics worth over Rs. 60.2 million concealed inside nine foreign postal parcels at the Central Mail Exchange in Colombo.
According to a statement issued by Sri Lanka Customs, the seized narcotics include Kush cannabis, hashish, ecstasy tablets and cocaine, with a total estimated street value of Rs. 60.265 million.
The parcels had arrived from Thailand, Spain, the United Kingdom and the United States and were identified during routine inspections of incoming international mail over the past few months.
Customs officers had detained the suspicious parcels pending collection by their intended recipients. However, as the recipients failed to collect them within the stipulated period, the parcels were examined in the presence of officers from the Police Narcotic Bureau (PNB).
The examination was conducted by officers of the Narcotics Control Unit (NCU) and Postal Appraising Branch of Sri Lanka Customs, together with PNB officers.
According to Customs, the seized narcotics included 4,934 grams of Kush cannabis valued at Rs. 49.34 million, 1,035 grams of hashish valued at Rs. 10.35 million, 25 grams of ecstasy tablets valued at Rs. 375,000 and four grams of cocaine valued at Rs. 200,000.
Of the nine parcels, three had arrived from Thailand, while two each originated from Spain, the United Kingdom and the United States.
Following preliminary investigations, Sri Lanka Customs handed over the seized narcotics to the Police Narcotic Bureau for further investigations and legal proceedings.
articles.summary: Sri Lanka Customs has seized narcotics worth over Rs. 60.2 million concealed inside nine foreign postal parcels at the Central Mail Exchange in Colombo.

The meeting also explored opportunities for cooperation to promote peace, reconciliation and friendship between the two countries, according to Tilvin Silva.

articles.title: Central Bank extends prohibited companies list to 27
articles.text:
The Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) has extended its list of prohibited pyramid schemes to 27, following the addition of Max App Media Ltd. and its affiliated companies.
In a statement issued today (28), the CBSL announced that investigations had determined that Max App Media Ltd., together with its affiliates Max LK (Pvt) Ltd. and Max Media Lanka (Pvt) Ltd., had engaged in, conducted and promoted a prohibited pyramid scheme.
The determination was made under Section 83(C) of the Banking Act, No. 30 of 1988, as amended.
Accordingly, the newly identified companies have been added to the Central Bank’s list of prohibited pyramid schemes, bringing the total number of companies and applications identified to 27.
The list also includes several previously identified entities, such as Tiens Lanka Health Care (Pvt) Ltd., Best Life International (Pvt) Ltd., Sport Chain, OnmaxDT, MTFE, Fastwin (Pvt) Ltd., Qnet/Questnet, Ledger Block, Beecoin App and TM App.
The Central Bank has published the updated list in a public notice issued through its Financial Consumer Relations Department, identifying the companies and applications determined to be prohibited schemes under the Banking Act.

articles.title: Flood warning for Gin Ganga basin extended by another 24 hours
articles.text:
The Irrigation Department has extended the flood warning issued for the Gin Ganga basin by another 24 hours, effective from 12.30 p.m. today (28).
According to the Department’s Hydrology and Disaster Management Division, the amber-level flood warning will remain in effect until 12.30 p.m. tomorrow (29).
The Department warned that people residing in flood-affected areas and motorists travelling along roads within these areas, particularly minor roads, should remain highly vigilant regarding the prevailing situation.
The warning was initially issued on October 26 and has been extended due to the continuing flood risk in the Gin Ganga basin.
The Irrigation Department has also requested Disaster Management authorities to take the necessary precautionary measures in this regard.

articles.title: Gotabaya’s travel ban: Court orders CID to appear on November 4
articles.text:
The Colombo Fort Magistrate’s Court today (28) ordered the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) to appear before court on November 4 to make submissions regarding a request to temporarily lift the overseas travel ban imposed on former President Gotabaya Rajapaksa.
Colombo Fort Magistrate Pasan Amarasena issued the order after considering a motion filed by the legal team representing the former President, seeking permission for him to travel to Singapore for further medical treatment.
The lawyers informed the court that Rajapaksa required further treatment in Singapore following heart surgery previously performed at a hospital in the country.
The former President was also present in open court when the matter was taken up.
However, the CID, which is the complainant in the case, was not present during the proceedings.
Accordingly, the Magistrate directed the CID to appear before court on November 4 to present its position on the request to temporarily lift the travel ban.
The overseas travel ban was imposed on former President Gotabaya Rajapaksa and several former intelligence officers in connection with investigations into the Easter Sunday terror attacks.

Accordingly, the Magistrate directed the CID to appear before court on November 4 to present its position on the request to temporarily lift the travel ban.

articles.title: Kawanthissa shooting: Two main suspects further remanded
articles.text:
The two main suspects arrested in connection with the shooting of iconic Sri Lankan tusker Kawanthissa have been further remanded until November 11.
The order was issued by the Mahawa Magistrate’s Court today (28), after the two suspects were produced before court.
On October 18, Police arrested a suspect believed to have been involved in the shooting of Kawanthissa during a joint operation conducted by the Walana Anti-Corruption Unit and the Department of Wildlife Conservation in the Galgamuwa area.
Two firearms were also recovered during the operation.
Kawanthissa, one of Sri Lanka’s most iconic wild tuskers, died on October 16 after battling serious health complications caused by a gunshot injury to his right front leg.
The tusker had been receiving veterinary treatment for several weeks before succumbing to his injuries.
articles.summary: The two main suspects arrested in connection with the shooting of iconic Sri Lankan tusker Kawanthissa have been further remanded until November 11. The order was issued by the Mahawa Magistrate’s Court today (28), after the two suspects were produced before court.

articles.title: UK and EU launch joint solar energy initiative in Colombo
articles.text:
The British High Commission in Colombo and the Delegation of the European Union to Sri Lanka have launched a joint solar energy initiative aimed at reducing carbon emissions and promoting sustainable energy practices.
The initiative was officially launched today (28) in the presence of Colombo Mayor Vraie Cally Balthazaar, British High Commissioner Andrew Patrick, EU Ambassador-designate Sylvia Hartleif and Deputy British High Commissioner Theresa O’Mahony.
According to the British High Commission, the project involves approximately 240 kilowatts-peak (kWp) of installed solar capacity across its office premises, which is expected to generate 365,000 kilowatt-hours (kWh) of electricity annually.
The initiative is projected to reduce carbon dioxide emissions by approximately 193 tonnes each year.
The launch included a ceremonial switch-on of the solar system and a showcase of other environmentally sustainable initiatives undertaken by the British High Commission.
The solar project forms part of broader efforts to reduce the High Commission’s environmental footprint through energy-efficient cooling, lighting and building systems, along with solar water heating. These measures are expected to save approximately 79,200 kWh of electricity annually.
Other sustainability initiatives include 10,000 litres of rainwater storage capacity, a vehicle fleet comprising 25% plug-in hybrid vehicles, and waste segregation, recycling and composting measures accounting for approximately 1.13 tonnes of waste annually.
British High Commissioner Andrew Patrick said the initiative demonstrates the shared commitment of the UK and European Union towards a cleaner future through practical cooperation.
Meanwhile, EU Ambassador-designate Sylvia Hartleif said the project reflects the European Union’s broader support for Sri Lanka’s Green Recovery, including the promotion of renewable energy, climate resilience and access to affordable, sustainable energy.
Deputy British High Commissioner Theresa O’Mahony emphasised that sustainability extends beyond solar energy to responsible water use, waste management and transportation practices.
The British High Commission stated that the initiative highlights the importance of international partnerships in advancing renewable energy and environmentally sustainable operations in Sri Lanka.
articles.summary: The British High Commission in Colombo and the Delegation of the European Union to Sri Lanka have launched a joint solar energy initiative aimed at reducing carbon emissions and promoting sustainable energy practices. The initiative was officially launched today (28) in the presence of Colombo Mayor Vraie Cally Balthazaar, British High Commissioner Andrew Patrick, EU Ambassador-designate Sylvia Hartleif and Deputy British High Commissioner Theresa O’Mahony.

articles.title: Krish case: Court decision on Namal’s bail application on November 3
articles.text:
The Colombo Magistrate’s Court today (28) announced that the decision on the bail application filed by Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa, who is currently in remand custody over the controversial Krish transaction, will be delivered on November 3.
Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama issued the order after considering submissions made by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) and the lawyers representing Rajapaksa.
The Parliamentarian has been remanded over allegations of accepting a bribe of Rs. 100 million in connection with the transfer of land at Transworks Square in Colombo Fort to the Krish company for a multipurpose development project.
The allegations relate to the acceptance of the payment in exchange for allegedly facilitating the transfer of the land to the company.

articles.title: Two arrested over black oil attack on SLTB bus in Ingiriya
articles.text:
Two individuals, including a private bus owner and a conductor, have been arrested for allegedly throwing black oil at a Sri Lanka Transport Board (SLTB) bus and assaulting its driver and conductor in Ingiriya.
According to reports, the incident occurred last night (27) in the Ketakerella area of Ingiriya, targeting an SLTB bus operating on the Karandana–Horana route under the Horana Depot.
The suspects in a three-wheeler had blocked the bus and reportedly thrown black oil at the driver through the front door of the bus before physically assaulting both the driver and conductor.
Following investigations into the incident, the Ingiriya Police arrested a private bus owner and a conductor in connection with the attack.
Further investigations are being conducted by the Ingiriya Police.

articles.title: Severe lightning warning issued across Sri Lanka
articles.text:
The Department of Meteorology has issued red alerts for severe lightning in three districts and amber alerts for 22 districts across Sri Lanka today (28).
According to the advisory issued by the Natural Hazards Early Warning Centre at 11.30 a.m., red alerts have been issued for the Monaragala, Ampara and Batticaloa districts, where thundershowers accompanied by severe lightning are likely.
Meanwhile, amber alerts have been issued for the remaining 22 districts, indicating the possibility of lightning activity.
The Department warned that temporary strong winds could also occur during thundershowers and urged the public to take necessary precautions to minimise damage caused by lightning.
The public has been advised to seek shelter indoors, avoid standing under trees and stay away from open areas such as paddy fields, tea plantations and open water bodies during thunderstorms.
People have also been urged to avoid using wired telephones, connected electrical appliances and open vehicles, including bicycles, tractors and boats.
The Department further cautioned the public to remain alert to fallen trees and power lines and to contact local disaster management authorities in emergencies.
The advisory remains valid until 11.30 p.m. today (28).
articles.summary: The Department of Meteorology has issued red alerts for severe lightning in three districts and amber alerts for 22 districts across Sri Lanka today (28). According to the advisory issued by the Natural Hazards Early Warning Centre at 11.30 a.m., red alerts have been issued for the Monaragala, Ampara and Batticaloa districts, where thundershowers accompanied by severe lightning are likely.

articles.title: Sri Lanka and Türkiye sign MoU to strengthen agricultural cooperation
articles.text:
Sri Lanka and Türkiye have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on Agricultural Cooperation, aimed at strengthening bilateral collaboration in agricultural development, modern farming technologies and food security.
The agreement was signed during a bilateral meeting between Sri Lanka’s Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Employment Arun Hemachandra and Türkiye’s Deputy Minister of Agriculture and Forestry Dr. Ahmet Bağcı in Ankara on Tuesday (27).
The discussions focused on several areas of mutual interest, including agricultural development, modern farming technologies, research and innovation, knowledge sharing and capacity building.
Particular attention was given to improving agricultural productivity, supporting farmers, promoting sustainable farming practices and strengthening food security in both countries.
The two sides also explored opportunities to strengthen cooperation between agricultural institutions in Sri Lanka and Türkiye, with an emphasis on implementing practical initiatives that would benefit their respective agricultural sectors.
The newly signed MoU establishes a framework for closer cooperation between the two countries in the agricultural sector.
Deputy Minister Hemachandra expressed appreciation for Türkiye’s commitment to strengthening bilateral relations and expanding cooperation in agriculture.
articles.summary: Sri Lanka and Türkiye have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on Agricultural Cooperation, aimed at strengthening bilateral collaboration in agricultural development, modern farming technologies and food security. The two sides also explored opportunities to strengthen cooperation between agricultural institutions in Sri Lanka and Türkiye, with an emphasis on implementing practical initiatives that would benefit their respective agricultural sectors.

articles.title: Johnston Fernando pleads guilty in luxury BMW tax fraud case
articles.text:
Former Minister Johnston Fernando has informed the Colombo Fort Magistrate’s Court that he pleads guilty to charges of possessing a luxury BMW vehicle imported into Sri Lanka without paying the required taxes and committing tax fraud.
According to reports, Fernando conveyed his position to the court through his lawyers in connection with the luxury vehicle that was found abandoned at a private hotel in Colombo.
The former minister was arrested by the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) on October 23 after recording a statement regarding the vehicle and was subsequently remanded.
The CID launched an investigation after receiving information about a black BMW bearing registration number WP C 24-0430, which had reportedly been parked at a hotel in Colombo a day before the Presidential Election.
Investigations revealed that the individual who had parked the vehicle had informed Police that it belonged to Johnston Fernando and had been brought to the hotel by his driver.
During an inspection of the vehicle, CID officers recovered several documents belonging to Fernando but found no documents relating to the vehicle’s registration.
Further investigations revealed that the registration number displayed on the BMW had been issued to a private company based in Nawala.
Meanwhile, Sri Lanka Customs confirmed that a vehicle bearing the BMW’s chassis number had not been legally imported into the country.
A subsequent examination conducted by the Government Analyst’s Department revealed that the vehicle had been illegally assembled.
Police investigations also uncovered possible links between the BMW and a luxury vehicle reported stolen in England in 2021.
According to Police, the vehicle had originally been manufactured in Germany and sold to a buyer in England, while its chassis and engine numbers were found to have links to the vehicle reported stolen in the United Kingdom.
articles.summary: Former Minister Johnston Fernando has informed the Colombo Fort Magistrate’s Court that he pleads guilty to charges of possessing a luxury BMW vehicle imported into Sri Lanka without paying the required taxes and committing tax fraud. According to reports, Fernando conveyed his position to the court through his lawyers in connection with the luxury vehicle that was found abandoned at a private hotel in Colombo.

articles.title: Family demands arrest of police officers over Homagama custody death
articles.text:
The family of a young man who died following his arrest by Homagama Police has lodged a complaint at Police Headquarters, demanding the immediate arrest of two police officers allegedly involved in assaulting him.
The victim’s wife said the family was seeking justice for her husband’s death, claiming that the officers concerned had only been suspended from duty and had not been arrested or subjected to legal action.
“We came to Police Headquarters to seek justice for what happened to my husband. The officers who assaulted and killed him have only been suspended. They have not been arrested. I want immediate legal action against them,” she said.
Speaking to the media outside Police Headquarters, a representative accompanying the family claimed that the Judicial Medical Officer had determined that the victim, identified as Ishara, died following injuries caused by blunt-force trauma.
According to the representative, the post-mortem findings revealed three fractured ribs, a fractured bone in the neck, brain swelling and bleeding in the head.
The representative said more than 48 hours had passed since Ishara’s death, but the officers allegedly responsible had still not been arrested.
The family also questioned the progress of investigations, claiming that officers attached to the Mirihana investigation unit had recorded statements from relatives but had failed to provide a satisfactory explanation for the absence of arrests.
They further claimed that a complaint had been lodged with the Human Rights Commission of Sri Lanka, but expressed dissatisfaction with the response so far.
The representative warned that the family and supporters would consider further action if the officers were not arrested by the following morning.
Meanwhile, the group also demanded justice for another young man, identified as Madhusanka, who was arrested alongside Ishara.
They alleged that Madhusanka, who is currently in remand custody, had also been assaulted by police and was in a serious condition.
They called for him to be immediately examined by a Judicial Medical Officer or admitted to a prison hospital.
The family and its supporters urged authorities to ensure an independent investigation and take legal action against anyone found responsible for Ishara’s death.
articles.summary: The family of a young man who died following his arrest by Homagama Police has lodged a complaint at Police Headquarters, demanding the immediate arrest of two police officers allegedly involved in assaulting him.

articles.title: CCTV captures gang attack on bus driver and conductor in Kalutara
articles.text:
A bus driver and conductor have been assaulted by a group of six individuals who blocked their bus using motorcycles in the Nagas Junction area of Kalutara.
According to Police, the incident occurred last evening (27) when the luxury bus, which had travelled from Colombo to Kalutara, was being taken home for parking after dropping off passengers.
Six individuals who arrived on three motorcycles had reportedly blocked the road, preventing the bus from proceeding, before physically assaulting the driver and conductor.
The assault was captured on a CCTV camera installed inside the bus.
Preliminary investigations revealed that the incident may have stemmed from an earlier dispute in Moratuwa, where the bus conductor had refused to allow an individual to board the bus while it was travelling towards Kalutara.
The conductor, who sustained injuries in the assault, has been admitted to the Kalutara Nagoda Teaching Hospital, with hospital sources indicating that his condition is somewhat serious.
The Kalutara North Police have launched investigations following a complaint regarding the incident and are taking steps to identify and apprehend those involved.
articles.summary: A bus driver and conductor have been assaulted by a group of six individuals who blocked their bus using motorcycles in the Nagas Junction area of Kalutara. Preliminary investigations revealed that the incident may have stemmed from an earlier dispute in Moratuwa, where the bus conductor had refused to allow an individual to board the bus while it was travelling towards Kalutara.

articles.title: Wanathavilluwa explosives case: ‘Gafoor Mama’ sentenced to 12 years in prison
articles.text:
Mohamed Shareef Adam Lebbe, alias ‘Gafoor Mama’, has been sentenced to 12 years of rigorous imprisonment after pleading guilty to charges related to the possession and collection of explosives and other prohibited materials at a property in Lactowatta, Wanathavilluwa.
The sentence was imposed by the Colombo Special Trial-at-Bar today (28), after the 63-year-old defendant, who is the third accused in the case, pleaded guilty to five charges filed against him.
The three-judge bench comprising Judges Lal Ranasinghe Bandara, Rashmi Singappuli and Naomi Wickramasinghe imposed a 12-year prison sentence for each of the five charges.
However, the sentences were ordered to run concurrently, resulting in a total imprisonment period of 12 years.
The court also ordered that the seven-and-a-half years the defendant had already spent in remand custody and under detention orders be deducted from his sentence. Accordingly, he will be required to serve approximately another four-and-a-half years in prison.
The judges stated that the sentence was determined after considering the defendant’s guilty plea, which avoided prolonging the trial, his age and other special circumstances.
Meanwhile, the sixth defendant in the case, Mohamed Rameez Mohamed Sajith, alias ‘Sajith Moulavi’, has requested time to inform the court whether he intends to plead guilty to the charges against him.
The court ordered that the case be taken up again tomorrow (29) at 8.00 a.m. and directed prison authorities to produce the sixth defendant before court by 7.45 a.m.
The court also ordered that special security be provided to ‘Gafoor Mama’ when he is produced before the Kegalle and Batticaloa High Courts, where two other cases against him are pending.
The Attorney General had filed 13 charges against six defendants in connection with the Wanathavilluwa explosives case.
It was revealed during today’s proceedings that five of the six defendants have already pleaded guilty and received their sentences, with the sixth defendant yet to inform the court of his position.

articles.title: Israel Election Results : Who is leading ?
articles.text:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s political bloc is leading with a projected 55 seats as more than half of the votes in Israel’s parliamentary election have been counted, according to the latest results reported by Al Jazeera.
Citing The Times of Israel, Al Jazeera reported that Netanyahu’s bloc is projected to secure 55 seats in the 120-member Knesset, while the opposition is expected to win 49 seats. Arab-led parties are projected to secure the remaining 16 seats.
Data from Israel’s Central Elections Committee shows that approximately 2.8 million ballots, representing 56% of the total, have been counted.
Netanyahu’s Likud party remains the largest individual party with 20.7% of the vote, followed by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party with 16.7%.
Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett’s Together alliance is in third place with 9%.
Despite leading the count, Netanyahu’s bloc remains six seats short of the 61 required to secure a parliamentary majority and form a government.
The latest figures suggest that coalition negotiations could be crucial in determining Israel’s next government.
The election comes amid deep political divisions over Netanyahu’s leadership, the Gaza war, regional security and demands for accountability over the October 7, 2023, attacks.
The results remain preliminary, with further changes possible as election officials continue counting ballots.
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s political bloc is leading with a projected 55 seats as more than half of the votes in Israel’s parliamentary election have been counted, according to the latest results reported by Al Jazeera.

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro flees to U.S. after losing Brazil election, sources say
articles.text:
Failed presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro has fled Brazil for the United States, which has confirmed it will grant him and his family entry visas.
It comes a day after Mr Bolsonaro vowed to remain in the South American nation to lead the political opposition against Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, known as Lula.
But over a three-day period, the far-right senator’s exact whereabouts and exit path out of Brazil have become shrouded in mystery.
Here is what we know about the timeline of his escape.
Saturday, October 24, local time: The idea of Senator Bolsonaro fleeing Brazil if he lost the presidential election was first raised by his brother, Eduardo, on a podcast. Eduardo suggested his brother was fearful of political persecution in Brazil amid ongoing corruption and money laundering investigations.
7pm, local Brazilian time, Sunday, October 25 (8am Monday AEST): Polls closed across Brazil after a two-hour voting extension was granted by Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin, following a request from President Lula’s campaign.
10pm, Sunday, October 25: The Tribunal Superior Electoral, Brazil’s electoral authority, announced Lula as the winner of the presidential election with 51.79 per cent of the vote, securing him a fourth term in office.
10:40pm, Sunday, October 25: Senator Bolsonaro delivered a three-minute address to the media near his electoral bunker in the Brazilian capital Brasília, saying he would not concede to Lula and would ask for the election result to be annulled.
3:45pm, local Washington DC time, Monday, October 26 (5:45am Tuesday AEST): US President Donald Trump told reporters he believed the Brazilian election had been “rigged” and said he believed the way it had been administered “looked very bad”.
5pm, local Brazilian time, Monday, October 26 (6am Tuesday AEST): Senator Bolsonaro posted an Instagram video claiming he was handed a court order for him to surrender his passports. He then promised to hand his documents over and stay in Brazil to spearhead the political opposition to Lula.
11am, Tuesday, October 27: Senator Bolsonaro missed the court deadline to turn in his passports — which were then cancelled — to federal police, according to police sources who spoke with Reuters. Local media and the AFP news agency reported the senator had not been seen at his residence in Brasilia throughout the morning. At about the same time, local media reports began to surface that the senator had fled Brazil on a plane destined for the US.
1:45pm, Tuesday, October 27: The leadership of President Lula’s Workers’ Party in Brazil’s lower house confirmed a preventative detention order has been filed and a request made for an INTERPOL red notice arrest alert to be issued worldwide for Senator Bolsonaro.
2:15pm, Tuesday, October 27: While Argentine officials denied Senator Bolsonaro entered the country from Brazil, local media reported a pilot confirmed a private jet was flown from Buenos Aires to the border town of Puerto Iguazú.
The pilot said he believed the jet was to pick up four passengers, including the senator. No confirmation was made that the aircraft then departed Argentina.
2:30pm, Tuesday, October 27: Mauricio Marcon, the deputy leader of Senator Bolsonaro’s Liberal Party, also said he believed Senator Bolsonaro had fled “into exile” in the US.
6:15pm, Tuesday, October 27: Re-elected President Lula described Senator Bolsonaro’s departure as “shameful” during his 81st birthday celebration in Brasilia. He said the senator treated Brazil as his “second country”, behind “licking American boots”.
“Those who are not liable do not fear. A fellow that secretly leaves his country, that’s because he is liable for something,” he said.
6:30pm, Tuesday, October 27: A senior official with the US State Department confirmed to the ABC that it would “issue visas to Flavio Bolsonaro and his family and allow them entry into the United States”.
10pm, Tuesday, October 27: Media outlets including CNN, The Washington Post and the BBC independently reported Senator Bolsonaro had landed in the US, quoting unnamed sources. The BBC reported he arrived in Florida, where he met his brother Eduardo.
There remains no official confirmation of Senator Bolsonaro’s arrival in the US, his location or the path he took to flee Brazil.
Local authorities continue to say there is no record of him crossing the border from Brazil into Argentina, and The Washington Post has also reported an anonymous Brazilian foreign ministry claim he may have passed through Venezuela. (ABC News)
articles.summary: Failed presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro has fled Brazil for the United States, which has confirmed it will grant him and his family entry visas. Saturday, October 24, local time: The idea of Senator Bolsonaro fleeing Brazil if he lost the presidential election was first raised by his brother, Eduardo, on a podcast.

articles.title: New fisheries training programme launched for youth in Puttalam and Ampara
articles.text:
A specialised training programme has been launched for young people from Puttalam and Ampara, aimed at creating new employment opportunities in Sri Lanka’s fisheries sector.
According to the German Embassy in Sri Lanka, the Department of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources, in partnership with DVV International Sri Lanka, has launched the first batch of the Longline Crew Member Training Programme at National Seafarers in Narahenpita, Colombo.
The programme combines practical training and simulation sessions conducted at the Southern Maritime Training Institute, providing participants with essential skills required to work in the longline fisheries industry.
The training also focuses on improving participants’ understanding of life at sea, including the responsibilities involved in working aboard fishing vessels.
The German Embassy stated that the initiative aims to equip young people with industry-relevant skills while creating new pathways to employment in Sri Lanka’s fisheries sector.
Further training batches are expected to be introduced as part of the programme, expanding opportunities for more young people to pursue careers in the industry.

articles.title: RTI Commission rules private telecom operators fall under RTI Act
articles.text:
The Right to Information (RTI) Commission of Sri Lanka has ruled that private telecommunications operators can fall within the scope of the Right to Information Act when providing services under government-issued licences.
The ruling, issued on October 21, came following an appeal seeking information about restrictions imposed on social media platforms and communication applications during March and April 2022.
The Commission examined whether telecommunications services provided by private companies constitute statutory or public functions under Section 43(g) of the RTI Act.
It determined that telecommunications services have a public character because they operate under government-issued licences, use state-controlled radio-frequency spectrum and provide essential communication infrastructure to the public.
The Commission observed that the private ownership of a telecommunications company does not automatically exempt it from the RTI Act.
It further noted that telecommunications operators function within a regulatory framework designed to protect public interests, consumer rights and the reliability of communication services.
The decision also referred to previous Court of Appeal rulings recognising that certain private entities performing public functions can be subject to the RTI Act.
However, the Commission clarified that the application of the RTI Act is limited to activities connected to an operator’s statutory or public functions under its telecommunications licence.
The ruling does not automatically require the disclosure of all requested information, as exemptions under the RTI Act may still apply.
A further hearing will determine whether documents relating to the 2022 Government imposed social media restrictions can be released.
articles.summary: The Right to Information (RTI) Commission of Sri Lanka has ruled that private telecommunications operators can fall within the scope of the Right to Information Act when providing services under government-issued licences. The Commission examined whether telecommunications services provided by private companies constitute statutory or public functions under Section 43(g) of the RTI Act.

articles.title: Airbus case: Court orders Namal Rajapaksa to be produced on November 19
articles.text:
The Permanent Trial-at-Bar of the Colombo High Court today (28) ordered that Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa, who is currently in remand custody over the controversial Airbus transaction, be produced before court through prison authorities on November 19.
The order was issued when Rajapaksa was produced before the Permanent High Court Trial-at-Bar today in connection with the case.
Rajapaksa was produced following an order issued by Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama on Tuesday (27), directing that he remain in custody until his appearance before the Trial-at-Bar.
The case relates to allegations of money laundering and accepting a Rs. 100 million bribe linked to the controversial Airbus transaction.
Indictments have been filed against Rajapaksa and three other individuals before the Permanent High Court Trial-at-Bar, with the approval of the Chief Justice.
Deputy Solicitor General Janaka Bandara informed the Colombo Chief Magistrate’s Court on Tuesday that the indictment contains 24 charges and lists 59 witnesses.
The Deputy Solicitor General also indicated that the proceedings before the Colombo Chief Magistrate’s Court were expected to conclude following the referral of the case to the Permanent High Court Trial-at-Bar.
Meanwhile, the Colombo Chief Magistrate previously ordered that a report on the proceedings before the Trial-at-Bar be submitted to the Magistrate’s Court on October 30.

articles.title: UAE honours Indian pilot for bravery during flydubai cockpit attack
articles.text:
The United Arab Emirates has honoured Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar and the flydubai crew for their courage during a cockpit incident on September 30 , when the seriously injured captain managed to open the cockpit door, allowing crew members and passengers to intervene and help avert a potential tragedy.
UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan conferred the First Class Order of Zayed II on the crew members involved in the incident. The honour recognises their efforts to protect passengers and secure the aircraft during the emergency.
The recognition comes amid widespread international praise for Machchhar, whose actions have drawn tributes from leaders in India, the UAE, Israel and the United States. Israel has also announced a civilian bravery award for the Indian captain, to be presented after he recovers from his injuries.
SHEIKH HAMDAN PRESENTS HONOURS
The honours were presented by Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister, Minister of Defence and Chairman of the Executive Council of Dubai.
Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed, in the presence of Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President, Prime Minister and Ruler of Dubai, also received the crew members on Tuesday.
The UAE leadership praised the crew’s courage and professionalism in protecting passengers and securing the aircraft, reaffirming that safeguarding people’s safety and security remains a priority for the country.
The crew members thanked the UAE President and expressed pride in receiving the honour.
Sheikh Hamdan had earlier visited Machchhar while he was receiving treatment for his injuries on October 3. Praising the captain’s courage and sense of responsibility, he said Machchhar had demonstrated the highest degrees of courage, responsibility and care for human life.
“From us, and from the leadership of the nation, he has our full appreciation and praise,” Sheikh Hamdan said in a social media post.
He added that the UAE was proud to have Machchhar as part of its team and national story, describing the country as “a nation of compassion … a nation of peace … and a nation of life”.
The visit followed the UAE General Civil Aviation Authority’s commendation of Machchhar, the crew and the passengers who helped bring the incident under control. (India Today)
articles.summary: The United Arab Emirates has honoured Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar and the flydubai crew for their courage during a cockpit incident on September 30 , when the seriously injured captain managed to open the cockpit door, allowing crew members and passengers to intervene and help avert a potential tragedy.

articles.title: Opposition calls for Speaker’s resignation, refuses to amend no-confidence motion
articles.text:
The Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) and Opposition MPs have called for the resignation of Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne, while declaring that they will neither amend nor withdraw the allegations contained in the no-confidence motion submitted against him.
In a joint statement issued by the Media Unit of the Office of the Leader of the Opposition, the MPs accused the government of attempting to prevent a parliamentary debate on the allegations against the Speaker.
The Opposition maintained that it was unethical for the Speaker to remain in office while an investigation by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) was underway, insisting that he should step down at least until the investigation is concluded.
The MPs strongly criticised the decision taken at the Committee on Parliamentary Business meeting on October 23, chaired by the Speaker, to reject the debate on the no-confidence motion unless the Opposition amended the allegations.
They alleged that the decision was influenced by the Speaker himself to prevent parliamentary scrutiny of the allegations against him.
According to the statement, the no-confidence motion was submitted to Parliament on October 9 and included in the Order Book on October 12.
At a Committee on Parliamentary Business meeting held on October 12 under the chairmanship of the Deputy Speaker, it had been proposed to seek the Attorney General’s opinion on whether the allegations contained in the motion could interfere with ongoing legal proceedings.
However, the Opposition alleged that the motion had not been referred to the Attorney General despite the agreement reached at the meeting.
The MPs also rejected the government’s argument that the allegations were sub judice, claiming that legal experts had found no basis for such a position.
They further pointed out that the allegations were based on a parliamentary inquiry report prepared following a letter from the Speaker’s Private Secretary.
The Opposition reiterated that it would not amend or withdraw the allegations to accommodate the government’s demands.
The statement further challenged the Speaker to either resign from office or face the 50 allegations contained in the no-confidence motion.
The Opposition warned that preventing the debate posed a serious threat to parliamentary democracy and the rights of Opposition MPs.
articles.summary: The Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) and Opposition MPs have called for the resignation of Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne, while declaring that they will neither amend nor withdraw the allegations contained in the no-confidence motion submitted against him.

articles.title: Seven fishermen missing in two separate incidents; Navy launches search operations
articles.text:
The Sri Lanka Navy has launched search operations to locate seven fishermen reported missing in two separate incidents off Mullaitivu and Matara.
According to the Navy Spokesman, three fishermen who had set out to sea from Puthukudiyiruppu in Mullaitivu on October 26 were reported missing by the owner of their fishing boat on Tuesday (27).
Following the report received by the Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre (MRCC) Colombo, the Navy deployed a vessel to conduct a search operation, while assistance was also sought from the Sri Lanka Air Force.
Accordingly, a Bell 212 helicopter was deployed today to assist in the search for the missing fishermen.
Meanwhile, four fishermen who had departed from Kudawella in Matara on October 21 were also reported missing by their boat owner on Tuesday (27).
The Navy Spokesman said MRCC Colombo was informed of the incident, following which a joint search operation was initiated.
A Navy vessel has been deployed to search for the missing fishermen, while assistance has also been requested from the Sri Lanka Air Force.
Search operations are continuing to locate the seven missing fishermen.

articles.title: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees as AI leads to efficiency push
articles.text:
Microsoft said Monday that it’s offering buyouts to a wide swath of employees as it strives to balance a costly artificial intelligence infrastructure build-out with capital efficiency.
The software maker announced a new voluntary exit offer for certain workers in the U.S., Canada, India and the United Kingdom at its experience level of 70 or below.
Around 60,000 people are eligible, according to a person familiar with the matter, who asked not to be named while discussing an internal matter. The effort affects about 27% of Microsoft’s total workforce of 223,000 people.
Microsoft has been ramping up spending on data centers to accommodate high AI computing demand, supplying cloud services to Anthropic, OpenAI and a slew of other companies. Capital expenditures for the September quarter should exceed $50 billion, Microsoft said in July. In the same quarter a year ago, capital spending and finance leases came to $34.9 billion.
That’s put a strain on Microsoft’s finances. In April, it announced a first-ever voluntary retirement program that around 7% of U.S. employees were eligible for. Then, in July, Microsoft announced plans to lay off 4,800 employees.
“The Voluntary Exit Offer reflects an important part of how we’re evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter,” Amy Coleman, Microsoft’s executive vice president and chief people officer, wrote in a memo to employees. “This builds on what we learned earlier this year through the Voluntary Retirement Program.”
Microsoft is in the midst of a business model transformation, increasingly trying to charge clients based on how much AI they actually use. It has armed programmers, sellers and supply chain workers with AI tools and observed noticeable results. At the same time, the 51-year-old maker of Windows and Office wants to ensure that it has the right talent to go after its most compelling new growth opportunities.
The idea is to make the shift without weakening Microsoft’s financial profile. In the second quarter, cloud rivals Alphabet and Amazon both reported negative free cash flow, but Microsoft showed $19.64 billion in positive free cash flow for the period, down 23% year over year.
Some marketing, sales and engineering teams have decided not to participate in the new buyout, the person said. Employees must decide whether to take the offer in early December, and those participating will leave on Dec. 31, the person added.
More than 30% of those who could join the voluntary retirement program went ahead with it, Microsoft said in July. But that was open to those at the senior director level of 67 and below, while the new initiative goes higher, to the vice president level, said the person briefed on the new plan. The person said Microsoft does not have a target in mind this time around.
On Wednesday, Microsoft is scheduled to report third-quarter results. (CNBC)
articles.summary: Microsoft said Monday that it’s offering buyouts to a wide swath of employees as it strives to balance a costly artificial intelligence infrastructure build-out with capital efficiency. Then, in July, Microsoft announced plans to lay off 4,800 employees.

articles.title: India issues medical insurance advisory for nationals travelling to UAE
articles.text:
The Indian Embassy in Abu Dhabi and the Consulate General of India in Dubai have issued an advisory urging Indian nationals travelling to or residing in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to ensure they have adequate medical insurance coverage.
In an advisory issued on Tuesday (27), the Indian diplomatic missions said they had received several reports of Indian nationals facing unexpected illnesses or medical emergencies that resulted in substantial medical bills beyond the financial capacity of patients and their families.
The missions noted that inadequate insurance coverage had contributed to the financial difficulties faced by those affected.
Accordingly, Indian nationals travelling to the UAE for tourism or other short-term visits have been advised to obtain appropriate medical insurance before commencing their journeys.
The insurance should also cover cashless medical treatment facilities and the cost of medical repatriation to India in the event of an emergency.
Meanwhile, Indian nationals residing in the UAE on employment visas or as dependents have been advised to verify that their existing insurance policies provide sufficient coverage for medical expenses in the UAE, as well as medical repatriation to India.

articles.title: Cyclone Arnab: Warning for fishermen as winds could reach 100 kmph
articles.text:
The Department of Meteorology has warned naval and fishing communities against venturing into several sea areas in the Bay of Bengal due to rough seas and strong winds associated with the very severe cyclonic storm ‘Arnab’, which is making landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast in India.
According to the Department, wind speeds in the sea areas between latitudes 10°N and 20°N and longitudes 80°E and 90°E could increase to 80–100 kmph, accompanied by heavy thundershowers.
Wave heights in these areas could reach 3–4 metres, resulting in very rough sea conditions.
Naval and fishing communities have been advised not to venture into the affected sea areas until further notice, while those already operating in these areas have been urged to move away.
Meanwhile, showers or thundershowers are expected at several places in the sea areas surrounding Sri Lanka today (28).
Southwesterly winds of 30–40 kmph are forecast, with speeds increasing to 60–65 kmph at times in the deep and shallow sea areas extending from Puttalam to Mullaitivu via Kankasanthurai and from Galle to Pottuvil via Hambantota.
Wind speeds in other sea areas around the island could increase to 50 kmph at times.
The sea areas from Puttalam to Mullaitivu and from Galle to Pottuvil are expected to become very rough at times, while other sea areas may also experience rough conditions.
Wave heights could increase to 2–2.5 metres in the sea areas off the coast from Matara to Pottuvil via Hambantota.
The Department further warned that temporary strong gusty winds of 60–70 kmph and very rough seas could occur during thundershowers.
Naval and fishing communities have been urged to remain attentive to future weather forecasts and advisories issued by the Department of Meteorology.
articles.summary: The Department of Meteorology has warned naval and fishing communities against venturing into several sea areas in the Bay of Bengal due to rough seas and strong winds associated with the very severe cyclonic storm ‘Arnab’, which is making landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast in India.

articles.title: CAA warns lubricant and grease traders over mandatory labelling requirements
articles.text:
The Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) has warned traders selling engine oil, gear oil, lubricants and grease to ensure that their products carry the mandatory Government Agreement Number, cautioning that legal action will be taken against those violating the regulations.
In a statement, the CAA said that under Direction No. 88, published in Gazette Extraordinary No. 2327/36 dated April 12, 2023, lubricants and grease cannot be imported or manufactured without a valid agreement with the Government of Sri Lanka.
Accordingly, every unit of lubricant or grease stored, stocked, sold, packed, repacked or displayed for sale must carry the number assigned to the relevant government agreement.
The number must be printed on the container, packaging or wrapper, or displayed on a firmly attached label.
The CAA emphasised that the requirement applies to retailers as well, even if they are not directly involved in importing or manufacturing the products.
Traders have been advised to verify the Government Agreement Number before purchasing stocks, obtain details of suppliers, importers or manufacturers, and retain purchase bills and invoices for verification.
They have also been instructed to inspect the labels of all lubricants and grease currently offered for sale to ensure compliance.
The CAA said market inspections and special raids are being conducted to identify violations, with legal action to be initiated against responsible parties following investigations.
Consumers can lodge complaints with the CAA through its hotline, 1977.
articles.summary: The Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) has warned traders selling engine oil, gear oil, lubricants and grease to ensure that their products carry the mandatory Government Agreement Number, cautioning that legal action will be taken against those violating the regulations.

articles.title: Sri Lanka seeks stronger UK trade and investment ties ahead of EXPO 2027
articles.text:
Sri Lanka has stepped up efforts to attract British investment and expand export opportunities through a series of recent business engagements in London and Dover ahead of Sri Lanka EXPO 2027, scheduled to take place in Colombo from January 14 to 17.
The Sri Lankan High Commission in London organised the programme recently, bringing together British investors, business leaders and representatives of key trade organisations.
The main event, the UK–Sri Lanka Trade and Investment Forum, was held at the High Commission, attracting more than 130 participants.
A high-level Sri Lankan delegation, led by Minister of Trade, Commerce, Food Security and Cooperative Development Wasantha Samarasinghe, attended the forum.
Addressing the gathering, Minister Samarasinghe encouraged British businesses to explore Sri Lanka’s export and investment opportunities, highlighting the benefits available under the UK’s Developing Countries Trading Scheme (DCTS).
Sri Lankan High Commissioner to the UK Nimal Senadheera stressed the importance of strengthening bilateral commercial relations and promoting EXPO 2027 as a platform for new business partnerships.
Export Development Board (EDB) Chairman and CEO Mangala Wijesinghe delivered a presentation on Sri Lanka EXPO 2027, outlining opportunities for international buyers and investors.
The forum featured discussions on sourcing Sri Lankan products, expanding commercial links with UK buyers and attracting foreign investment.
Representatives from Marks & Spencer, the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka (BOI), the Ministry of Industries and Entrepreneurship Development and the private sector participated in the discussions.
Investment opportunities in Port City Colombo, real estate and other sectors were also highlighted.
The Sri Lankan delegation also held discussions with the UK–Sri Lanka Chamber of Commerce on strengthening business cooperation and encouraging British participation in EXPO 2027.
The delegation met Samantha Cohen, Chief Executive of the Commonwealth Enterprise and Investment Council (CWEIC), to explore opportunities for connecting Sri Lankan businesses with international investors through Commonwealth business networks.
The programme concluded with a business networking event in Dover, organised jointly with RS Rock Holdings, which brought together more than 30 UK business representatives, including potential investors.
According to the Sri Lankan High Commission, the engagements were aimed at strengthening commercial partnerships and encouraging British buyers, investors and business representatives to visit Colombo for EXPO 2027.
The High Commission said it expects the exhibition to provide further opportunities for trade, investment and business cooperation between Sri Lanka and the United Kingdom.

articles.title: Ranil calls for closer economic ties with India to secure Sri Lanka’s place in new world order
articles.text:
Former President Ranil Wickremesinghe has called for stronger economic cooperation with India, describing it as a key priority for Sri Lanka as global political and economic power shifts towards Asia.
Addressing the 50th webinar of the International Chamber of Commerce Sri Lanka (ICCSL), Wickremesinghe said Sri Lanka must adapt to emerging geopolitical realities through technological modernisation, regional economic integration and stronger partnerships with major powers.
He identified closer economic cooperation with India as one of the main requirements for Sri Lanka to secure its position in the emerging global order.
Wickremesinghe highlighted India’s growing economic influence, describing it as the dominant power in the Bay of Bengal region and referring to its position among the world’s three largest economies by GDP.
He said the Indian Ocean would become one of the centres of the new global order, driven by the economic rise of Asia and Africa.
The former President also pointed to the growing economic potential of the Bay of Bengal, with India playing a central role alongside Indonesia, Bangladesh and other emerging regional economies.
He said Sri Lanka should strengthen relations with Bay of Bengal countries and Southeast Asia, eventually working towards greater regional economic integration.
Wickremesinghe also referred to Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s remarks at the NDTV World Summit, where Modi described the current global situation as a transition between two world orders.
According to Wickremesinghe, Modi had highlighted the increasing use of finance, trade, technology and shipping as instruments of geopolitical influence.
He also referred to Modi’s quotation of the ancient Indian strategist Chanakya on the need to prevent Matsya Nyaya, or the law of the fishes, under which the strong swallow the weak.
“We in Sri Lanka must adapt to these changes, or we will be swallowed up by bigger fish,” Wickremesinghe warned.
The former President said technological advancement was becoming central to national sovereignty, with the United States and China emerging as the two leading powers in artificial intelligence and computing.
He stressed that Sri Lanka must undertake economic and social transformation based on technological modernisation to remain competitive.
Outlining his proposals, Wickremesinghe called for Sri Lanka to become a maritime logistics centre, strengthen economic cooperation with India and build closer relationships with countries across the Bay of Bengal and Southeast Asia.
He also proposed that Sri Lanka join BRICS and strengthen relations with the United States, China, Russia and Japan.
The former President urged a review of the effectiveness of regional organisations, including the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) and the Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC).
He also called for accelerating the work of the Colombo Security Conclave, which he said would play an important role in the future security of the Indian Ocean.
Wickremesinghe stressed the importance of developing a technologically advanced Sri Lankan Navy equipped with small and medium-sized vessels, while prioritising the protection of undersea communication cables.
He warned that Sri Lanka could lose its relevance in the emerging global order unless it embraced economic modernisation and stronger regional partnerships.
“Either we go this way, or we fade into insignificance, like one of the small Pacific islands,” he said.
articles.summary: Former President Ranil Wickremesinghe has called for stronger economic cooperation with India, describing it as a key priority for Sri Lanka as global political and economic power shifts towards Asia. He identified closer economic cooperation with India as one of the main requirements for Sri Lanka to secure its position in the emerging global order.

articles.title: UK issues fresh security update for Middle East travellers
articles.text:
The United Kingdom has issued heightened travel warnings for parts of the Middle East, cautioning British nationals about the risk of sudden regional escalation and possible flight cancellations, airspace closures and travel disruptions.
The UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) updated its travel advice on Tuesday (October 27), warning that the security situation in the region remains highly unpredictable.
“The context in the Middle East remains deeply unpredictable and the risk of sudden escalation is high,” the advisory said.
The updated guidance also applies to British nationals planning to travel through the region, including passengers transiting through major Middle Eastern aviation hubs.
Travellers have been advised to monitor developments closely, check with airlines before departure and prepare for possible changes to travel arrangements.
The warnings come amid heightened regional tensions and recent security measures affecting diplomatic missions.
According to the FCDO, Iran has previously stated its intention to target locations associated with the United States and Israel, including businesses, organisations and facilities.
The advisory noted that strikes and retaliatory attacks have already affected civilian and US military infrastructure across the region. British nationals have been urged to avoid areas near military and security facilities, follow local authorities’ instructions and keep their departure plans under review. GOV.UK +1
The latest warnings follow a US State Department decision on October 21 ordering non-emergency government employees and their family members to leave Saudi Arabia amid attacks by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi movement.
US officials clarified that the mandatory departure order applied only to Saudi Arabia, although other diplomatic missions in the region have adjusted staffing arrangements.
The UK advisory does not indicate that all Middle Eastern airspace is currently closed but warns that airports and airspace could be shut at short notice.
The developments have raised concerns about international air travel, particularly for passengers using Gulf aviation hubs to connect between Asia, Europe and other destinations.
articles.summary: The United Kingdom has issued heightened travel warnings for parts of the Middle East, cautioning British nationals about the risk of sudden regional escalation and possible flight cancellations, airspace closures and travel disruptions. articles.title: Namal’s lawyer seeks bail citing parents’ serious health conditions
articles.text:
President’s Counsel Ali Sabry, appearing for remanded Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa, has urged the Colombo Chief Magistrate’s Court to grant bail to his client on compassionate grounds, citing the serious health conditions of his parents, former President Mahinda Rajapaksa and former First Lady Shiranthi Rajapaksa.
According to court reports, Sabry made the submissions when a motion filed on behalf of Namal Rajapaksa in connection with the Krrish transaction case was taken up before Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama.
Sabry told the court that Namal’s 81-year-old father had recently returned home after being hospitalised due to severe depression, while his mother was suffering from a serious heart condition.
He said Shiranthi Rajapaksa was hospitalised and scheduled to undergo open-heart surgery at 4 p.m. on Tuesday.
The lawyer argued that Namal, as the eldest son, had a responsibility to care for his parents and urged the court to consider their health conditions as exceptional grounds for bail.
Sabry also cited the constitutional presumption of innocence and argued that everyone should be treated equally before the law.
He questioned why a government minister facing a case filed by the Bribery Commission had not been produced before a Magistrate’s Court.
Referring to compassionate considerations in other cases, Sabry noted that the government had cared for the parents of former LTTE leader Velupillai Prabhakaran following his death.
He argued that the circumstances involving Namal’s parents justified his release on bail, adding that presenting more exceptional circumstances would require inventing them.
Meanwhile, the Bribery Commission informed the court that it had not received the relevant documents concerning the fresh bail application and requested time to present its position.
The commission also rejected allegations of unequal treatment, maintaining that it applied the law equally to everyone.
After considering the submissions, the Chief Magistrate directed the Bribery Commission to present its position on the fresh bail application on Wednesday (28).
Namal Rajapaksa remains in remand custody in connection with the Krrish transaction case.
Separately, the court ordered prison authorities to produce him before the Colombo Permanent Trial-at-Bar on October 28 in connection with the SriLankan Airlines Airbus transaction case, in which 24 charges have been filed against the accused.

articles.title: 5 player managers sign MOUs with Sri Lanka Cricket under new regulations
articles.text:
Five player managers have signed Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs) with Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) under a newly introduced policy aimed at regulating player management and preventing outside interference in cricket affairs, according to information received by Newswire.
However, despite the introduction of the new accreditation system, only existing player managers have qualified so far, according to SLC Cricket Transformation Committee member Roshan Mahanama.
Speaking at a press conference in Colombo, Mahanama expressed disappointment that the accreditation process had so far attracted only those already involved in player management.
“Unfortunately, only those who were already there have qualified so far,” Mahanama said, encouraging other eligible individuals to register as player managers under the new policy.
According to SLC, nearly 30 individuals had applied for accreditation as player managers, but only five qualified under the criteria, all of whom were already involved in player management.
The agreements formally recognise the individuals as SLC-accredited player managers, allowing them to represent cricketers in specified matters while imposing restrictions on their involvement in cricket administration and team selection.
According to the MOU, accredited managers will be permitted to coordinate with SLC on player registrations, travel arrangements, accommodation, welfare, contractual compliance, media appearances and commercial commitments.
However, the agreement prohibits player managers and players from organising or participating in collective actions intended to improperly influence SLC officials, selectors or other cricket authorities.
The MOU also allows SLC to suspend or revoke accreditation for violations of its regulations, misconduct or breaches of the agreement.
Under the new framework, player managers must submit written confirmation from each cricketer they represent, while SLC will recognise only one accredited manager per player at a time.
Mahanama said the policy was developed after studying similar regulations implemented by Cricket Australia and the Pakistan Cricket Board.
“We obtained the policies of Cricket Australia and the Pakistan Cricket Board. After studying both, we developed a policy suitable for Sri Lanka,” Mahanama said.
He explained that members of the committee, including its legal representatives, had worked with SLC’s legal and international departments to finalise the agreement.
Mahanama said the agreements had been signed approximately two weeks earlier.
Meanwhile, committee member and former Sri Lanka cricketer Sidath Wettimuny warned that player managers must not interfere in cricket-related matters, particularly team selection.
“We have told the players not to bring their managers to the cricket board. Keep them away from us,” Wettimuny said.
He clarified that SLC had no objection to cricketers appointing personal managers but stressed that their involvement must remain within permitted limits.
“There is no problem with having a player manager, but do not get involved in cricket affairs, selection affairs or anything like that,” he said.
Wettimuny further warned that players themselves could face scrutiny if their managers became involved in such matters.
“If that happens, we will be looking at the players’ conduct,” he said.
However, Wettimuny said the committee had not encountered such problems so far.
articles.summary: Five player managers have signed Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs) with Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) under a newly introduced policy aimed at regulating player management and preventing outside interference in cricket affairs, according to information received by Newswire. However, despite the introduction of the new accreditation system, only existing player managers have qualified so far, according to SLC Cricket Transformation Committee member Roshan Mahanama.
