articles.title: SLC introduces random alcohol & drug testing as part of new player discipline measures
articles.text:
Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) has introduced stricter fitness and disciplinary measures for national players, including random alcohol and drug testing and closer monitoring of their diets, Sri Lanka Cricket Transformation Committee member Sidath Wettimuny has revealed.
Speaking at a press conference, Wettimuny said the board was implementing several new initiatives to improve players’ fitness, discipline and overall professionalism.
He said players are now subjected to weekly skinfold measurements to monitor body fat levels and are provided with individual fitness routines.
“We are doing things which we have never done before. Every week our players are tested for skinfold measurements and they are given a routine of what they have to do,” Wettimuny said.
He said improvements were already visible on the field, with players appearing fitter, more agile and focused.
Wettimuny also revealed that the players’ eating habits had been identified as a major concern.
“Food, diet has been a huge problem according to Gary. Our guys do not eat the kind of food they need to eat,” he said.
To address the issue, SLC has appointed a dietician to closely monitor players’ meals, both in Sri Lanka and during overseas tours.
Wettimuny said dietary instructions were even being communicated directly to hotels accommodating the national team to ensure players followed their prescribed meal plans.
The same dietary and fitness requirements are also being applied to players preparing for upcoming Test assignments.
Meanwhile, Wettimuny confirmed that SLC has begun introducing alcohol and drug testing as part of its efforts to strengthen player discipline.
“We have also started doing alcohol testing or drug testing or whatever,” he said.
He added that players would be informed about random checks going forward.
“Random checks on alcohol content, whatever. We are doing that also to make sure the players stay focused on the game and don’t step out of line,” Wettimuny said.
He emphasised that discussions with players also covered smoking, alcohol consumption, nutrition and other aspects of professional conduct.
According to Wettimuny, the new measures are intended to ensure that players maintain the fitness, discipline and professionalism required to perform consistently at international level.

articles.title: ‘This must stop’: Amnesty slams Sri Lanka’s proposed Organised crime Bill
articles.text:
Amnesty International has called on the Sri Lankan government to immediately withdraw the proposed Prevention of Organised Crimes Bill, warning that it would grant authorities sweeping powers and undermine fundamental human rights.
In a statement issued on Tuesday (27), the international human rights organisation described the proposed legislation as one of the most alarming laws introduced by the National People’s Power (NPP) government.
Amnesty warned that the Bill could allow suspects to be detained for up to two years without trial, permit confessions made to senior police officers to be used as evidence in court, and restrict media reporting on court proceedings.
It also raised concerns over provisions allowing police to conduct searches without warrants and obtain personal information, including telephone records, subscriber identities and device location data, without a court order.
“This extraordinary bill is the most alarming in a string of repressive laws proposed by the National People’s Power (NPP) government. It reintroduces most of the very worst elements of the PTA and applies them to a wide range of offences,” said Smriti Singh, Amnesty International’s South Asia Director.
The organisation warned that the proposed law could recreate conditions that previously enabled arbitrary detention, torture and other human rights abuses under Sri Lanka’s Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA).
According to Amnesty, the legislation would allow suspects to be detained for up to one year before being charged, followed by a further year in pretrial detention.
The organisation also expressed concern that courts could consider a person’s clothing, tattoos, hand signs, language, associations and places visited when determining whether they belong to an organised criminal group.
Amnesty warned that such provisions could encourage discriminatory profiling and undermine the right to a fair trial.
Another major concern involves provisions allowing confessions made to police officers above the rank of Assistant Superintendent to be admitted as evidence.
The organisation said the proposed law would also place the burden on accused persons to prove that torture or other ill-treatment had occurred.
Amnesty further criticised provisions requiring individuals to provide information to police, with penalties of up to seven years in prison or a fine of Rs. 200,000 for failing to comply.
The organisation warned that access to telecommunications and digital records without judicial oversight could expose journalists’ sources, lawyers’ communications and organisers of lawful protests to surveillance.
“Sri Lanka is following a dangerous path by introducing legislation that weakens safeguards against torture and other ill-treatment and that puts fair trial guarantees at risk, repeating the mistakes of the PTA. This must stop,” Singh said.
Amnesty called on the government to withdraw the legislation entirely and initiate meaningful public consultations on measures to combat organised crime while protecting fundamental rights.
The call follows similar concerns raised by the Human Rights Commission of Sri Lanka and the Bar Association of Sri Lanka, both of which have urged the government to withdraw the proposed legislation.
The government has maintained that the proposed legislation is intended to strengthen efforts against organised criminal networks and support international cooperation in combating serious crime.
The Bill was gazetted on October 6 and presented to Parliament on October 20, where it remains at the first-reading stage.
articles.summary: Amnesty International has called on the Sri Lankan government to immediately withdraw the proposed Prevention of Organised Crimes Bill, warning that it would grant authorities sweeping powers and undermine fundamental human rights. Amnesty called on the government to withdraw the legislation entirely and initiate meaningful public consultations on measures to combat organised crime while protecting fundamental rights.

articles.text:
The third phase of the Baseline Road Extension Project in Colombo was officially launched today (27) under the patronage of Deputy Minister of Urban Development Eranga Gunasekara.
The project involves widening and upgrading a 0.86-kilometre stretch of road from Kirulapone Junction to Dutugemunu Street along the Colombo–Horana main road.
The government has allocated Rs. 2.886 billion in domestic funding for the project, which will be implemented by the Road Development Authority under the Ministry of Transport, Highways and Urban Development.
The upgraded road will feature six lanes, each 3.5 metres wide, along with dedicated pedestrian walkways and bicycle lanes.
Construction is expected to be completed within 18 months, with the road scheduled to open to the public in April 2028.

articles.title: Parliament to debate revised no-confidence motion against Speaker on November 3
articles.text:
A debate on the revised no-confidence motion against Speaker of Parliament Jagath Wickramaratne, to be submitted by the Opposition, has been scheduled for Tuesday, November 3.
According to a statement issued by Parliament, the debate was included in the parliamentary business scheduled for the first week of November.
Parliament is scheduled to meet from November 3 to 6, with the agenda finalised at a meeting of the Committee on Parliamentary Business held on October 23, chaired by Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne.
On Wednesday, November 4, Parliament will debate regulations published in Extraordinary Gazette No. 2508/27 under the Imports and Exports (Control) Act, along with a Supplementary Estimate, from 11.30 a.m. to 5.00 p.m.
A government-sponsored Adjournment Motion will subsequently be debated from 5.00 p.m. to 5.30 p.m.
On Thursday, November 5, a debate on another Adjournment Motion moved by the government has been scheduled from 11.30 a.m. to 5.30 p.m.
Meanwhile, Friday, November 6, has been allocated for debates on several Private Members’ Motions from 11.30 a.m. to 5.00 p.m.
These include proposals to increase train services on the Puttalam Railway Line, introduce a systematic programme for planting and maintaining trees along road reserves, and convert all Colleges of Education in Sri Lanka into university faculties.
Other motions concern the introduction of smart grids and smart meters, improving swimming skills, designating Udawalawe as a tourist zone, and controlling the spread of common water hyacinth.
An Adjournment Motion moved by the Opposition will be debated from 5.00 p.m. to 5.30 p.m. on Friday.
According to Parliament, on each sitting day, the period from 9.30 a.m. to 10.00 a.m. will be allocated for business under Standing Orders 22(1) to 22(6), followed by Questions for Oral Answers from 10.00 a.m. to 11.00 a.m. and Questions under Standing Order 27(2) from 11.00 a.m. to 11.30 a.m.

articles.title: Cyclone Arnab’s impact on Sri Lanka expected to ease from Wednesday
articles.text:
The impact of Very Severe Cyclonic Storm ‘Arnab’ on weather conditions across Sri Lanka is expected to gradually decrease from tomorrow (28), according to the Department of Meteorology.
In its latest weather forecast, the Department said the cyclone was located approximately 800 kilometres northeast of Kankasanthurai at 11.30 a.m. today (27), over the west-central Bay of Bengal.
The system, centred near latitude 16.2°N and longitude 83.7°E, is expected to cross the Indian coast through Andhra Pradesh as a very severe cyclonic storm around 11.30 a.m. tomorrow (28).
Meanwhile, several spells of showers are forecast in the Western and Sabaragamuwa provinces and in the Kandy, Nuwara Eliya, Galle and Matara districts.
Showers or thundershowers are also expected at a few places in the Uva Province and the Batticaloa and Ampara districts after 1.00 p.m.
Strong winds of approximately 40–50 kmph can be expected at times over the western slopes of the Central Hills, the Northern, North-Central and North-Western provinces, and the Trincomalee and Hambantota districts.
According to the weather forecast for major cities on October 28, Batticaloa is expected to record the highest maximum temperature of 33°C, followed by Anuradhapura, Colombo, Ratnapura and Trincomalee at 31°C.
Nuwara Eliya is forecast to record the lowest minimum temperature of 15°C, with a maximum of 18°C.
The Department of Meteorology has advised the public to take adequate precautions against temporary strong winds and lightning during thundershowers.

articles.title: Nearly 40% of Sri Lanka’s fish production lost to post-harvest wastage
articles.text:
Nearly 40% of Sri Lanka’s annual fish production is lost due to post-harvest wastage, it was revealed during a discussion chaired by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake at the Presidential Secretariat today (27).
According to the President’s Media Division, Sri Lanka’s annual fish production stands at approximately 400,000 metric tonnes, with a significant proportion lost after harvesting.
The issue was highlighted during discussions on the 2027 Budget proposals of the Ministry of Fisheries, Aquatic and Ocean Resources, where attention was drawn to measures needed to minimise wastage and improve the efficiency of the fisheries sector.
President Dissanayake also instructed officials to prepare comprehensive plans to transform the fisheries industry into a commercially viable sector, while increasing production and improving the incomes of fishing communities.
The discussion also focused on measures to make fish products available to consumers at fair and affordable prices, as part of the government’s efforts to reduce the cost of living.
Attention was drawn to the operations of the Ceylon Fisheries Corporation and the Peliyagoda Central Fish Market Complex, including existing operational challenges and the need for improved infrastructure.
The President also highlighted the importance of introducing modern fishing vessels to strengthen deep-sea fishing, while officials discussed opportunities for private-sector investment in the industry.
Meanwhile, President Dissanayake instructed Finance Ministry officials to develop loan schemes specifically suited to the fisheries sector, taking into account the industry’s unique challenges.
The meeting also examined sustainable coastal infrastructure development, green harbour projects and measures to expand aquaculture in Sri Lanka.

articles.title: New national committee to address wildlife hazards to aviation safety
articles.text:
The Cabinet of Ministers has approved the establishment of a National Wildlife Hazard Management Committee for Aviation Safety to minimise the risk of collisions between aircraft and wildlife in Sri Lanka.
The committee will serve as a national coordination mechanism for managing wildlife-related hazards in civil aviation, with representation from all relevant stakeholder institutions.
The proposal was submitted by the Minister of Ports and Civil Aviation in line with Sri Lanka’s obligations under the Convention on International Civil Aviation, also known as the Chicago Convention.
According to the government, the Convention requires member states to implement measures to identify, assess and minimise wildlife strike hazards at airports and surrounding areas.
These measures include recording and reporting aircraft-wildlife collisions, collecting information on potentially hazardous wildlife and conducting continuous risk assessments by qualified personnel.
Reports of wildlife strikes must also be submitted to the International Civil Aviation Organization’s (ICAO) Bird Strike Information System.
The government said ICAO guidelines for the Asia-Pacific region provide for the establishment of national wildlife hazard management committees or forums to facilitate coordinated action on aviation safety.
The proposed committee is expected to strengthen coordination among relevant authorities in addressing wildlife-related risks to aircraft operations.
articles.summary: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved the establishment of a National Wildlife Hazard Management Committee for Aviation Safety to minimise the risk of collisions between aircraft and wildlife in Sri Lanka. The committee will serve as a national coordination mechanism for managing wildlife-related hazards in civil aviation, with representation from all relevant stakeholder institutions.

articles.title: Sri Lankan students to get education and job opportunities in South Korea
articles.text:
The Cabinet of Ministers has approved a new agreement aimed at providing Sri Lankan students with higher education opportunities in South Korea, followed by employment prospects and opportunities for long-term residence.
Under the proposed Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), Sri Lankan students selected through the National Institute of Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH) will be able to pursue higher education at Changshin University in South Korea.
The programme also aims to facilitate employment opportunities in industries located in South Korea’s Gyeongsangnam-do Province, along with opportunities for long-term residence in the province.
According to the government, a new MoU and operational framework have been prepared involving five parties: Sri Lanka’s Ministry of Labour, the National Institute of Occupational Safety and Health, South Korea’s Gyeongsangnam-do Province, the Sacheon Chamber of Commerce and Industry, and Changshin University.
The initiative follows an earlier MoU signed between NIOSH and Changshin University in 2023 to implement vocational training and student exchange programmes.
However, the previous agreement could not be implemented due to issues concerning certain provisions, prompting the preparation of a revised agreement and operational framework.
The Cabinet has approved the proposal submitted by the Minister of Labour to proceed with the new agreement involving the five parties.
